subject: Velocity demo — performance qualification rundown & MAP
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@velocity.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@velocity.ai>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Velocity demo — preliminary performance recap & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for carving out time today to walk through the integration and demo. Quick recap from Redwood's side while the details are fresh. I captured a short SLO checklist and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) below — attaching an editable checklist and the session recording.

Top-level asks we heard from you:
- Target 95th latency goal for end-user completions: ~200ms (for short, single-shot queries).
- Sustained throughput: ~150–200 req/s for peak daytime traffic; ability to burst to 700–800 for short spikes.
- Concurrent streaming sessions: up to 350 concurrent live streams (WebRTC-like consumer flows).
- First-byte streaming latency: sub-50ms preferred for live audio/gallery experiences.

Our immediate assessment (post-demo):
- Baseline model variant demonstrated ~180ms p95 on 16k prompt slices in our session for similar prompt size when served on our dedicated pool.
- Streaming first-token median was ~30–40ms on wired networks in the demo environment; tail increases on cellular were visible.
- We recommend the following SLO candidates to start qualification: p95 latency <= 220ms, sustained throughput 200 req/s, burst to 800 req/s, concurrent streams 350 with degrade-to-graceful-fallback policy.

Proposed MAP (owners + target dates):
1) Shared SLO checklist + measurement plan — Redwood (Mateo) to send instrumentation guide and prometheus/grafana dash templates — target: 2028-06-28.
2) Pilot traffic run (stage) with synthetic traffic to validate throughput & concurrency — Velocity to define traffic pattern; Redwood to run pilot — target run: 2028-07-05.
3) Latency tail investigation under mixed prompt lengths — Redwood (Mateo & Jonas) — report back with mitigation options (KV cache, batching knobs, quantized variant) — target: 2028-07-10.
4) Failure/fallback playbook (graceful degrade to lower-capacity model + region failover) — joint doc — target: 2028-07-12.

Attachments: Velocity-SLO-checklist.xlsx (Excel) and demo-recording-20280625.mp4 (link).

Next step: Mateo will follow up with the instrumentation guide and the editable checklist by EOD Wednesday. Can you confirm: (a) the 95th p95 <=220ms is acceptable as an initial bar, and (b) you can provide a representative traffic dump or synthetic pattern for the pilot by 2028-07-01?

Cheers,

— Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@velocity.ai>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya@velocity.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Velocity demo — preliminary performance recap & next steps

Thanks, Soojin — appreciated the clear write-up and the recording. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the clip with platform ops: 

- p95 target: 220ms is fine as a starting point. Ultimately product wants to hold p90 ~120ms for the simplest card-type queries, but we understand tail behavior will vary by prompt.
- Throughput: confirmed — daytime sustained ~180 req/s, night batch ~30 req/s. Bursts can hit 700+ for launches; we'll provision headroom for that.
- Streaming: first-byte <=50ms is the bar for our interactive experience; if mobile introduces 2x tail we need a fallback plan.

We can provide synthetic traffic patterns and a 72-hour sample of production traces (anonymized) by 2028-06-30. I'll share the S3 link to the trace dump.

Two asks for Redwood before we lock the pilot window: 
1) A short doc that lists exactly what instrumentation we need from our side (metrics names, quantiles, and traces) so our infra team can wire it up.
2) Confirmation of the model variant you'll run during the pilot (so we can compare apples-to-apples).

I'll loop in ops (ops@velocity.ai) in the next note.

— Alex
Head of Platform, Velocity.ai
alex.nguyen@velocity.ai

Subject: Re: Velocity demo — preliminary performance recap & next steps

Alex — thanks for the quick response and for the traces offer. I grabbed the checklist Soojin attached and sketched an instrumentation template inline below. We'll push the editable checklist to the Drive link and include metric names.

Short instrumentation primer (what we need from Velocity):
- request.latency_ms: histogram (p50, p90, p95, p99) — label by model_variant, region, prompt_len_bucket
- streaming.first_byte_ms: histogram (p50, p95, p99) — label by network_type (wifi/cellular) if available
- request.success_rate: counter + error labels (code, model_variant)
- concurrent.streams: gauge by region
- tokens.per_request: gauge/histogram to help size KV cache
- trace_id header propagation for 1% sampled distributed traces (Zipkin/OTLP link)

Pilot plan notes:
- We'll run two 3-hour synthetic windows and one sustained 24-hour mixed traffic run. The synthetic windows will push to 1.1x and 3x your peak to validate autoscale.
- For the pilot we'll use model_variant: redwood-v1-8k-quant (same as demo) and measure a secondary quantized variant redwood-v1-q4_8k for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Deliverables + owners:
- Instrumentation guide + Prometheus targets — Mateo (2028-06-28)
- Drive with editable SLO checklist and demo clips — Soojin (today)
- Pilot execution & initial telemetry report — Redwood Ops (Jonas + Mateo) (post-run +72h)

I don't see blockers from our side. Alex — if Velocity can drop the trace dump by 6/30 we'll aim to start pilot week of 7/3.

-Mateo
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
